title: Zepto Targets $3 Billion IPO Valuation, Less Than Half Its Peak
excerpt: The quick-commerce startup has begun anchor investor discussions at a sharp markdown from its $7 billion private valuation, with a possible delay looming if the gap with institutional buyers can't be bridged.
body:
• Zepto is targeting a post-money IPO valuation of roughly $3 billion (₹29,100 crore), less than half the $7 billion it commanded in its October 2025 private round.
  • The anchor book is set at ₹2,298 crore, with a proposed fresh issue of ₹5,000 crore and an indicative price of ₹18.76 per share.
  • Some domestic mutual funds remain unconvinced, pushing for a further 30–40% valuation cut before committing capital.
  • Zepto may delay its listing if the valuation gap with investors isn't closed before its IPO papers expire on August 21.

Zepto has begun discussions with prospective anchor investors for its IPO at a post-money valuation of roughly $3 billion — a brutal markdown from the $7 billion the Aadit Palicha-led quick-commerce startup was worth just nine months ago, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

The pre-money valuation under discussion is approximately $2.5 billion (₹24,000 crore), with an indicative share price of ₹18.76. The proposed offering includes a fresh issue of ₹5,000 crore and a small offer-for-sale component of about ₹106 crore, significantly scaled back from the ₹8,010 crore fresh issue and 113.47 million share OFS outlined in Zepto's updated draft red herring prospectus filed last month.

A Valuation in Freefall

The descent has been steep and swift. In October 2025, Zepto raised $450 million from investors including the California Public Employees' Retirement System (CalPERS), General Catalyst, and Lightspeed at a $7 billion valuation. By mid-July, foreign institutional investors were evaluating the company at a pre-money valuation of about $4.5 billion, implying a post-money valuation of roughly $5.1 billion. Now, the number has cratered further to $3 billion.

Even in the unlisted market, the rout is visible. Zepto shares are trading at approximately ₹39 apiece — valuing the company at about $5.1 billion — down 33% from March levels, according to data from UnlistedZone.com cited by Bloomberg.

The anchor book, set at ₹2,298 crore, accounts for nearly 45% of the total issue size. The remaining allocation is split across a ₹1,532 crore qualified institutional buyers (QIB) book, a ₹766 crore high-net-worth individual portion, and a ₹511 crore retail tranche, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

Mutual Fund Resistance

The $3 billion target may still be too rich for some buyers. Several domestic mutual funds remain unconvinced by the proposed pricing, arguing it does not adequately reflect Zepto's business profile and profitability outlook, according to Analytics Insight. Fund managers are reportedly seeking a further 30–40% reduction before committing capital.

"The lack of another high-traffic vertical makes it difficult for Zepto to have valuations at par with those of its peers."

— Market participants, as reported by Analytics Insight

A central concern: Zepto's limited business model. Unlike Swiggy and Eternal's Blinkit — both of which operate large food-delivery verticals alongside quick commerce — Zepto remains a single-vertical play. That narrower revenue base, combined with persistent cash burn, has made institutional investors cautious, especially after a string of new-age tech IPOs that underperformed post-listing.

Delay on the Table

If the valuation gap can't be bridged, Zepto is considering delaying the listing entirely, Inc42 reported, citing an Economic Times report. The company has received formal price indications from large institutional investors and is negotiating before deciding whether to proceed. Its draft prospectus remains valid until August 21 — a tight window that leaves little room for extended haggling.

SEBI approved the IPO in April. Norway's sovereign wealth fund Norges and Motilal Oswal had earlier expressed interest at a higher valuation band and were expected to account for 40–45% of the anchor book, according to Moneycontrol. Whether those allocations hold at the revised pricing remains unclear.

Competitors Cheer

Shares of Swiggy and Eternal both jumped as much as 4% following reports of Zepto's valuation reset, according to Outlook Business. The logic is straightforward: a capital-constrained Zepto would have less firepower for the discount wars and dark-store expansion that have defined quick-commerce competition in India.

Market participants see the lower valuation as a signal that public investors are no longer willing to bankroll aggressive cash burn in exchange for top-line growth — a dynamic that could benefit incumbents already under pressure to demonstrate profitability.

What It Means for Diaspora Investors

For NRI investors who rode India's startup boom through private placements and pre-IPO stakes, Zepto's markdown is a case study in the growing gap between private-market exuberance and public-market discipline. The $7 billion-to-$3 billion slide underscores the repricing risk embedded in late-stage private rounds — particularly for companies that have yet to prove a path to profitability.

Looking Ahead

The next three weeks are decisive. Zepto must either secure anchor commitments at a price both sides can live with or let its August 21 deadline pass and refile later — absorbing the reputational cost of a postponed debut. The outcome will set the tone for how public markets price India's remaining cohort of quick-commerce and consumer-tech unicorns still waiting in the IPO pipeline.
nri_angle: Zepto's $7 billion-to-$3 billion valuation slide is a cautionary signal for NRI investors in India's private startup market, highlighting the widening gap between late-stage private pricing and what public markets will actually pay.
author: Diaspora Desk
